task_title: The smoke teardown consults the DELETE status before rmtree and treats 409 like 429 (AUG-117 recurrence)
task_criteria:
PASS: the smoke teardown consults the DELETE status before it removes the namespace directory - the only shutil.rmtree in the helper sits after the 200/404 guard.
PROOF: grep -n "if st not in (200, 404)" tests/smoke.sh prints line 103 and grep -n "shutil.rmtree" tests/smoke.sh prints line 105, so the guard precedes the rmtree.
FAILIF: the rmtree line number is not greater than the guard line number, or either pattern is absent from tests/smoke.sh.

PASS: the helper's namespace root falls back to auger's own resolver instead of a hardcoded legacy path.
PROOF: grep -c 'AUGER_NS_ROOT") or auger.namespaces_base()' tests/smoke.sh prints 1.
FAILIF: a count of 0, or the fallback is a hardcoded path string that auger never writes to.

PASS: the hermetic teardown proof is collected and green on the fixed tree.
PROOF: python3 -m pytest tests/test_smoke_teardown.py -q prints "11 passed".
FAILIF: any failed or errored node, a collection error, or a pass count other than 11.

PASS: the three ROOT-coupling tests pass, including the non-vacuous 409 keep test.
PROOF: python3 -m pytest tests/test_smoke_teardown.py -q -k 'root_follows or root_prefers or actually_writes' prints "3 passed".
FAILIF: fewer than 3 passed or any failure.

PASS: the ROOT coupling was falsified against the pre-fix helper and the transcript is committed.
PROOF: grep -c "3 failed" evidence/REVIEW-AUGER-006-r2/01-red.txt prints 1 and git ls-files evidence/REVIEW-AUGER-006-r2/01-red.txt prints the path.
FAILIF: the transcript is absent, untracked, or records no red run.

PASS: the throwaway sweep still covers the pytest leak class and spares fresh and foreign namespaces.
PROOF: python3 -m pytest tests/test_smoke_teardown.py -q -k sweep prints "5 passed".
FAILIF: fewer than 5 passed, any failure, or a collection error.

PASS: the gate pytest arm names the proof file, so the gate and CI execute it.
PROOF: grep pytest tests/gate.sh | grep -c test_smoke_teardown.py prints 1.
FAILIF: a count of 0 or a count above 1.

items.criterion:
PASS: the smoke teardown consults the DELETE status before it removes the namespace directory - the only shutil.rmtree in the helper sits after the 200/404 guard.
PROOF: grep -n "if st not in (200, 404)" tests/smoke.sh prints line 103 and grep -n "shutil.rmtree" tests/smoke.sh prints line 105, so the guard precedes the rmtree.
FAILIF: the rmtree line number is not greater than the guard line number, or either pattern is absent from tests/smoke.sh.
items.detail: Ran the exact greps: `grep -n "if st not in (200, 404)" tests/smoke.sh` -> `103:    if st not in (200, 404):`; `grep -n "shutil.rmtree" tests/smoke.sh` -> `105:    shutil.rmtree(os.path.join(ROOT, ns), ignore_errors=True)` (single occurrence). 105 > 103, and tests/smoke.sh:103-104 returns `False, f"DELETE returned HTTP {st}"` before the rmtree, so a refused DELETE never removes the directory.

items.criterion:
PASS: the helper's namespace root falls back to auger's own resolver instead of a hardcoded legacy path.
PROOF: grep -c 'AUGER_NS_ROOT") or auger.namespaces_base()' tests/smoke.sh prints 1.
FAILIF: a count of 0, or the fallback is a hardcoded path string that auger never writes to.
items.detail: `grep -c 'AUGER_NS_ROOT") or auger.namespaces_base()' tests/smoke.sh` -> `1` (tests/smoke.sh:44 `ROOT = os.environ.get("AUGER_NS_ROOT") or auger.namespaces_base()`). The fallback is the product resolver defined at auger.py:483-491 (DUCKBRAIN_NAMESPACES_PATH -> DUCKBRAIN_DATA_DIR/namespaces -> legacy default); no hardcoded legacy path string remains in smoke.sh (grep for AUGER_NS_ROOT shows only the comment at :38 and the ROOT line at :44).

PASS: the three ROOT-coupling tests pass, including the non-vacuous 409 keep test.
PROOF: python3 -m pytest tests/test_smoke_teardown.py -q -k 'root_follows or root_prefers or actually_writes' prints "3 passed".
FAILIF: fewer than 3 passed or any failure.
items.detail: `python3 -m pytest tests/test_smoke_teardown.py -q -k 'root_follows or root_prefers or actually_writes' -v` -> `collected 11 items / 8 deselected / 3 selected` / `3 passed, 8 deselected in 0.36s`, exit_code 0. Selected nodes are test_helper_root_follows_auger_data_dir_on_a_200, test_persistent_409_keeps_the_directory_where_auger_actually_writes and test_helper_root_prefers_duckbrain_namespaces_path. The 409 keep test is non-vacuous: it asserts the directory under auger.namespaces_base() survives a persistent 409 with its data, then flips the script to 200 and requires that SAME directory gone (tests/test_smoke_teardown.py, non-vacuity tail).

PASS: the ROOT coupling was falsified against the pre-fix helper and the transcript is committed.
PROOF: grep -c "3 failed" evidence/REVIEW-AUGER-006-r2/01-red.txt prints 1 and git ls-files evidence/REVIEW-AUGER-006-r2/01-red.txt prints the path.
FAILIF: the transcript is absent, untracked, or records no red run.
items.detail: `grep -c "3 failed" evidence/REVIEW-AUGER-006-r2/01-red.txt` -> `1` (tail: `3 failed, 8 deselected in 0.28s`, `pytest exit code: 1`, with the three FAILED node ids named). `git ls-files evidence/REVIEW-AUGER-006-r2/01-red.txt` -> `evidence/REVIEW-AUGER-006-r2/01-red.txt` (tracked; the whole r2 evidence dir is tracked). The transcript header records the pre-fix tree (HEAD 7872eef, smoke.sh untouched) and the failures are the ROOT-derivation assertions, e.g. `AssertionError: the helper claimed removal but the directory under auger's own tree (auger.namespaces_base()) survived`.

items.criterion:
PASS: the throwaway sweep still covers the pytest leak class and spares fresh and foreign namespaces.
PROOF: python3 -m pytest tests/test_smoke_teardown.py -q -k sweep prints "5 passed".
FAILIF: fewer than 5 passed, any failure, or a collection error.
items.detail: `python3 -m pytest tests/test_smoke_teardown.py -q -k sweep` -> `.....  [100%]` / `5 passed, 6 deselected in 0.47s`, exit_code 0. The five nodes cover auger-pytest-* stale reap, ghost row (row without directory), fresh directory spared, foreign prefixes spared, and the original auger-smoke-/auger-eval- classes; THROWAWAY at tests/smoke.sh:36 includes "auger-pytest-".

items.criterion:
PASS: the gate pytest arm names the proof file, so the gate and CI execute it.
PROOF: grep pytest tests/gate.sh | grep -c test_smoke_teardown.py prints 1.
FAILIF: a count of 0 or a count above 1.
items.detail: `grep pytest tests/gate.sh | grep -c test_smoke_teardown.py` -> `1`. The match is the real arm at tests/gate.sh:212 (`setsid timeout ... python3 -m pytest ... tests/test_smoke_teardown.py ...`); the other mention at :206 is a comment and does not match the `pytest` grep. Also pinned by test_gate_arm_runs_this_file in tests/test_smoke_teardown.py (part of the 11-passed run).

items.criterion: The 409 ladder is bounded and a persistent 409 is reported (never reinterpreted as deletion), with the directory and its data intact.
items.detail: tests/smoke.sh:88-105: drop() loops `for attempt in range(len(conflict_backoffs) + 1)` and breaks when `st != 409 or attempt == len(conflict_backoffs)`, then returns `False, f"DELETE returned HTTP {st}"` without rmtree. Run: `python3 -m pytest tests/test_smoke_teardown.py -q -k 'persistent_409 or transient_409' -v` -> `3 passed, 8 deselected in 0.32s`, exit_code 0; test_teardown_survives_a_persistent_409_with_the_directory_intact asserts d.is_dir(), decision.json still "[]", delete count == ladder+1, and "409"/"teardown skipped" in stdout.

items.criterion: The 429 contract is preserved: a 429 teardown is retried exactly once by the caller and the directory is only removed after a 200/404.
items.detail: tests/smoke.sh:155-158 keeps `if not ok and "HTTP 429" in why: ok, why = drop(ns)` (one re-entry), and drop() rmtree's only after the 200/404 guard. Verified by an ad-hoc probe (/tmp/probe429.py) that runs the REAL extracted heredoc against a stub whose DELETE answers [429, 200]: stdout `namespace auger-smoke-429probe removed`, calls `[db GET, delete 429, delete 200]`, `dir exists after: False`, rc 0. Note: no committed test exercises the 429 path (only a docstring mention at tests/test_smoke_teardown.py:187), but the behaviour is correct.

items.criterion: The sweep's 24h/prefix guards are not weakened: fresh throwaways and foreign namespaces are never deleted.
items.detail: tests/smoke.sh:118-131 keeps the `cutoff = time.time() - 24*3600` test and the `n.startswith(THROWAWAY)` gate. Run: `python3 -m pytest tests/test_smoke_teardown.py -q -k sweep` -> `5 passed, 6 deselected in 0.47s`, including test_sweep_spares_a_fresh_pytest_directory (no deletes, dir survives) and test_sweep_never_takes_a_foreign_prefix (auger-prod-one/releases/auger untouched, "no stale" printed).

items.criterion: The hermetic rig exercises the real helper code (extracted from smoke.sh) rather than a copy, so the tests cannot pass against a divergent reimplementation.
items.detail: tests/test_smoke_teardown.py:110-121 _heredoc_body() extracts the single `<<'PY'` heredoc from the real tests/smoke.sh (asserts exactly one heredoc and that `def drop(` is present) and the rig executes it as a subprocess; the stub serves the REAL auger.namespaces_base() loaded from REPO_ROOT/auger.py via AUGER_REAL_AUGER (STUB_AUGER tail, raising RuntimeError if the path is not a file). Confirmed by the 11-passed run and by the red transcript, which used the same extraction against the pre-fix smoke.sh and got 3 failed.
